title: Research in Low-Resource Settings and Community-Based Participatory Research

hook.en: Many studies are designed for well-funded hospitals with expensive machines. Most patients in the world, including most in Pakistan, are not in such places. Good research is not only for rich labs: with the right question, a partnership with the community and simple, honest methods, a small clinic can produce knowledge that matters.
hook.ur: Bohat se studies aise madad-yafta aspatalon ke liye design hote hain jahan mehngi machinein hon. Duniya ke zyada tar mareez, Pakistan ke bhi, aisi jagahon par nahi. Achhi research sirf ameer labs ke liye nahi: sahi sawal, bradari ke saath shirakat aur saade, imaandar tareeqon se chhota clinic bhi ahem ilm paida kar sakta hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll ask questions that matter locally, use simple and affordable methods, work with a community as partners using CBPR, protect participants where resources and literacy are limited, and share findings in ways that help.
goal.ur: End tak aap muqami taur par ahem sawal poochhenge, saade aur sasta tareeqe istemal karenge, bradari ke saath CBPR se shareek ban kar kaam karenge, wasail aur taleem mehdood hone par shirkat karne walon ko mehfooz rakhenge, aur findings ko aise tareeqe se share karenge jo madad karein.

text.en: **Research in low-resource settings** often asks questions that high-income studies ignore: how to deliver rehabilitation with few therapists, how to adapt exercise to home and family life, what works with low literacy, or what patients can afford. **Community-based participatory research (CBPR)** treats community members as **partners**, not subjects: they help choose the question, design the methods, collect data, interpret results and use them. This improves relevance, trust and the chance that findings are used.
text.ur: **Kam wasail wale halaat mein research** aksar aise sawal poochhti hai jinhein ameer mulkon ke studies nazar-andaaz karte hain: kam therapists ke saath rehabilitation kaise dein, exercise ko ghar aur khandan ki zindagi se kaise milayein, kam taleem walon ke saath kya kaam karta hai, ya mareez kya afford kar sakte hain. **Community-based participatory research (CBPR)** bradari ke afraad ko **shareek** samjhti hai, tajurbe ke mauzu nahi: woh sawal chunne, tareeqe banane, data jama karne, nateeje samajhne aur unhein istemal karne mein madad karte hain. Isse mutabiqat, bharosa aur findings ke istemal hone ka imkaan behtar hota hai.

text.en: Think of **designing a bridge**. Engineers can sit in an office and draw, but a bridge that villagers helped plan fits where they actually walk, uses the materials they can maintain and is protected because it is theirs. CBPR is building research with the community instead of for it.
text.ur: **Pul ka design** sochein. Engineer daftar mein baith kar naqsha bana sakte hain, lekin jis pul ke plan mein gaon walon ne madad ki woh wahin banta hai jahan woh asal mein chalte hain, woh saman istemal karta hai jo woh sambhal sakte hain, aur woh mehfooz rehta hai kyunke unka apna hai. CBPR bradari ke liye nahi, bradari ke saath research banana hai.

title.en: Doing research the usual way versus with the community
title.ur: Aam tareeqe se research aur bradari ke saath research

rows.en: The researcher decides from the literature
rows.ur: Muhaqqiq literature se tay karta hai

rows.en: Community members and patients help to name what matters
rows.ur: Bradari ke afraad aur mareez batane mein madad karte hain ke kya ahem hai

rows.en: Tools adapted in local language, culture, literacy and cost
rows.ur: Muqami zubaan, saqafat, taleem aur kharch ke mutabiq dhale hue aale

rows.en: Trained local members help, with fair pay and support
rows.ur: Trained muqami afraad madad karte hain, munsifana ujrat aur madad ke saath

rows.en: Shared discussion with community members before finalising
rows.ur: Aakhri karne se pehle bradari ke afraad ke saath mushtarak baat cheet

rows.en: Also a local-language summary, a community meeting and a poster in the clinic
rows.ur: Saath muqami zubaan ka khulasa, bradari ki mulaqat aur clinic mein poster

question.en: A researcher plans to test a home exercise programme for stroke survivors in a rural area. Which first step best fits a community-partnered approach?
question.ur: Muhaqqiq dehi ilaqe mein stroke se bachne walon ke liye ghar ki exercise programme aazmane ka plan banata hai. Bradari ke shareek tareeqe ke liye behtareen pehla qadam kaun sa hai?

text.en: Meet stroke survivors, carers and community leaders to ask what matters, what is possible at home and what would make the programme usable
text.ur: Stroke se bachne walon, dekhbhal karne walon aur bradari ke rehnumaon se milein aur poochhein kya ahem hai, ghar par kya mumkin hai aur kya programme ko istemal ke qabil banayega

feedback.en: Yes — listen first, then design together.
feedback.ur: Haan — pehle suniye, phir milkar design karein.

text.en: Translate a programme from a foreign study without changes
text.ur: Kisi bairooni study ka programme bina tabdeeli ke tarjuma kar dein

feedback.en: It may not fit the setting.
feedback.ur: Yeh jagah ke liye fit na ho.

text.en: Ask only hospital staff what to do
text.ur: Sirf aspatal ke staff se poochhein kya karna hai

feedback.en: Patients and carers know daily life best.
feedback.ur: Mareez aur dekhbhal karne wale roz ki zindagi sab se behtar jaante hain.

question.en: An information sheet and consent form are written in dense English for participants who read little. What is the problem and the fix?
question.ur: Maloomati sheet aur razamandi ka form ghane angrezi mein likha hai un shirkat karne walon ke liye jo kam parhte hain. Masla aur hal kya hai?

text.en: No problem; they can ask someone else to read it
text.ur: Koi masla nahi; woh kisi aur se parhwa sakte hain

feedback.en: That may not give them real choice.
feedback.ur: Is se haqeeqi ikhtiyar nahi milta.

text.en: Consent will not be informed; use plain Urdu or the local language, pictures, a verbal explanation and checking understanding by asking them to explain it back
text.ur: Razamandi batayi hui nahi hogi; saada Urdu ya muqami zubaan, tasveerein, zabani wazahat aur unse dohrane ko keh kar samajh jaanchna istemal karein

feedback.en: Yes — consent must be understood, not just signed.
feedback.ur: Haan — razamandi samjhi honi chahiye, sirf dastakhat shuda nahi.

question.en: Your study has almost no budget and no special equipment. Which design is realistic?
question.ur: Aap ke study ka budget taqreeban nahi aur khaas aala nahi. Kaun sa design haqeeqat pasand hai?

text.en: Do not do research at all
A small audit, a survey, a case series or a pilot with simple measures such as a stopwatch, tape and short questionnaire, done well and reported honestly
text.ur: Chhota audit, survey, case series ya saade naap (stopwatch, fita, chhota questionnaire) wala pilot, achhi tarah kiya aur imaandari se report kiya

feedback.en: Yes — good questions and care matter more than expensive tools.
feedback.ur: Haan — achhe sawal aur ehtiyat mehngay aalon se zyada ahem hain.

text.en: A large multicentre trial with imaging

feedback.en: That needs resources you do not have.
feedback.ur: Is ke liye wasail chahiye jo aap ke paas nahi.

text.en: **Parachute research: arriving, collecting data and leaving.** Studies that take data from a community and give nothing back damage trust and may harm people. Share the results in plain language, leave behind something useful (training, a tool, a service) and give credit to local partners. Another trap is copying a high-income design that cannot be sustained locally: choose measures and programmes the community can afford to continue.
text.ur: **Parachute research: aana, data jama karna aur chale jana.** Jo studies bradari se data le kar kuch wapas nahi dete woh bharosa nuqsan dete hain aur logon ko nuqsan pohancha sakte hain. Nateeje saade alfaaz mein share karein, kuch mufeed (training, aala, khidmat) chhor jayein aur muqami shareekon ko credit dein. Ek aur jaal ameer mulkon ka aisa design copy karna hai jo muqami taur par qaim na rah sake: aise naap aur programme chunein jin ko jari rakhna bradari afford kar sake.

text.en: **Start with the questions your patients already ask.** Keep a list of the problems that come up again and again: cost of transport, missing exercises, fear of surgery, advice from relatives. Ask your patients and a local community leader which of these they would most like solved, and design a small, practical study or audit around one. Share what you learn in a short Urdu summary on the clinic wall.
text.ur: **Un sawalon se shuru karein jo aap ke mareez pehle se poochhte hain.** Un masail ki fehrist rakhein jo baar baar aate hain: aamad-o-raft ka kharch, exercises chhoot jana, surgery ka khauf, rishtedaron ka mashwara. Apne mareezon aur kisi muqami rehnuma se poochhein ke in mein se kaun sa sab se pehle hal ho, aur ek par chhota, amali study ya audit design karein. Jo seekha woh clinic ki deewar par mukhtasar Urdu khulase mein share karein.

question.en: Can small studies in low-resource settings still count as good research?
question.ur: Kya kam wasail ke chhote studies phir bhi achhi research maane ja sakte hain?

answer.en: Yes, if the question is clear, the methods fit the question and the reporting is honest about limits. Local knowledge fills gaps that large international studies leave, and pilot results can guide the design of bigger work. Reporting guidelines such as STROBE and CARE apply equally. What matters is rigour and relevance, not the size of the budget.
answer.ur: Haan, agar sawal saaf ho, tareeqe sawal se milte hon aur report hadon ke baare mein imaandar ho. Muqami ilm woh khalaein bharta hai jo bade beinul-aqwami studies chhor dete hain, aur pilot ke nateeje bade kaam ke design ki rehnumai kar sakte hain. STROBE aur CARE jaisi reporting guidelines barabar lagu hoti hain. Ahem sakhti aur mutabiqat hai, budget ka size nahi.

beats.patient: A physiotherapist in a district hospital notices that many women stop pelvic floor exercises after delivery because of shame, lack of privacy and family duties. She forms a small group with local women, a female health worker and a village elder.
beats.assessment: The patients' own words show the main barriers, which the therapist had not guessed.
beats.treatment: Together they design a private, short home programme with pictures, deliver it through the female health worker, and measure leakage with a simple diary and a short questionnaire.
beats.reassess: After six months more women are following the programme, the group presents the findings in a community meeting, and the district health office asks to copy the approach.

text.en: **Protect participants whose power is low.** People with little education, money or standing may feel unable to refuse researchers or officials. Keep participation truly voluntary, never link it to access to care, protect privacy in small communities where everyone knows everyone, pay fairly for time and travel, and have a plan if someone is harmed or discloses abuse.
text.ur: **Un shirkat karne walon ko mehfooz rakhein jin ka ikhtiyar kam ho.** Kam taleem, paisa ya martabe wale log muhaqqiqon ya afsaron ko inkaar na kar paane ka mehsoos kar sakte hain. Shirkat ko haqeeqatan apni marzi ki rakhein, care tak rasai se kabhi na jorein, chhote ilaqon mein jahan sab ek doosre ko jaante hain nijiyat mehfooz rakhein, waqt aur safar ka munsifana muawza dein, aur plan rakhein agar kisi ko nuqsan ho ya zyadati ka zikr kare.

text.en: A review of community-based research by Israel and colleagues described the principles of partnership approaches: recognising the community as a unit of identity, building on strengths, facilitating collaborative involvement in all phases, integrating knowledge with action for mutual benefit, and a long-term commitment. Wallerstein and Duran showed how community-based participatory research can address health disparities by sharing power and resources between community and academic partners, while noting that it requires time and trust and that it can be difficult to do well.
text.ur: Israel aur saathiyon ke community-based research ke review ne shirakat ke tareeqon ke usool bayan kiye: bradari ko pehchan ki ikai maanna, khoobiyon par tameer, tamam marahil mein mushtarak shirkat ki sahulat, ilm ko amal se mutual faide ke liye jorna, aur taweel muddat ki wabastagi. Wallerstein aur Duran ne dikhaya ke community-based participatory research bradari aur academic shareekon ke beech taqat aur wasail baant kar sehat ke farq ko hal kar sakti hai, jabke yeh bhi likha ke is mein waqt aur bharosa chahiye aur isay achhi tarah karna mushkil ho sakta hai.

text.en: **Ask, Adapt, Partner, Share back.** Ask what matters locally, adapt methods, partner with the community and share results back.
text.ur: **Poochhein, Dhalein, Shareek, Wapas dein.** Poochhein muqami taur par kya ahem hai, tareeqe dhalein, bradari ke shareek bane, aur nateeje wapas share karein.

summary.en: Low-resource research asks locally relevant questions and uses simple, affordable, honest methods.
summary.ur: Kam wasail wali research muqami taur par ahem sawal poochhti hai aur saade, sasta, imaandar tareeqe istemal karti hai.

summary.en: CBPR treats the community as partner in choosing the question, collecting data and using results.
summary.ur: CBPR bradari ko sawal chunne, data jama karne aur nateeje istemal karne mein shareek samajhti hai.

summary.en: Protect low-power participants, explain consent in plain language and always share results back.
summary.ur: Kam ikhtiyar walon ko mehfooz rakhein, razamandi saade alfaaz mein samjhayein aur nateeje hamesha wapas share karein.

back.en: Researchers arrive, collect data and leave without giving anything back.
back.ur: Muhaqqiq aate hain, data jama karte hain aur kuch wapas diye baghair chale jate hain.

front.en: How do you check consent with low literacy?
front.ur: Kam taleem mein razamandi kaise jaanchein?

back.en: Plain language, pictures, a verbal explanation and asking them to explain it back.
back.ur: Saadi zubaan, tasveerein, zabani wazahat aur unse dohrane ko kehna.

front.en: What matters most in small studies?
front.ur: Chhote studies mein sab se ahem kya hai?

back.en: Rigour and relevance, not budget size.
back.ur: Sakhti aur mutabiqat, budget ka size nahi.

note.en: A small study any clinic can do.
note.ur: Chhota study jo har clinic kar sakta hai.
